definition: A surrogate is one who stands in and acts in another's place, with that person's role and authority borrowed for the occasion.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word surrogate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know surrogate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: When the ambassador fell ill on the eve of the treaty, her deputy attended the signing as a surrogate, initialing each page on her behalf.
A messenger is weaker than a surrogate: the messenger only carries the absent person's words, while a surrogate is trusted to act — to answer, sign, and decide in their place.
A double goes further than a surrogate — a surrogate openly stands in for someone, while a double is meant to pass as the person, so that onlookers never know a substitution happened.

A proxy is the narrow, procedural version — someone authorized to cast your vote or sign in your absence, often just a name on a form. A surrogate steps further into the role, acting and speaking as the person across a whole occasion.

A stand-in fills a spot so the work can go on — a body under the lights while the star is in makeup — and carries no authority to decide anything. A surrogate carries the absent person's authority: what the surrogate says or signs counts as theirs.

So the campaign dispatched a trusted surrogate to each region: veteran allies who took the stage in her place, delivered her positions, and answered hostile questions on her behalf.
These were not couriers reading a fixed script.
Each was briefed for hours and authorized to commit the campaign to specific local promises.
